newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares fall, off lows on support.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares fall, off lows on support.

text.p: Istanbul shares posted losses in in volatile trade on Thursday, as they recouped part of their losses after diving on the cancellation of a law allowing the government to sell state property, brokers said.

The IMKB-100 closed 1,005.29 points, or 1.09 percent lower at 90,823.50. Afternoon volatility caused daily trade volume to leap to 17.01 trillion lira ($163.3 million) from Wednesday's 13.69 trillion ($131.8 million).

The index sank 2.5 percent in the afternoon on news that the constitutional court annulled a law that would enable the government to sell state property as part of its measures to raise funds to plug deficits.

"Panic sales, mainly in shares of largely state owned firms were sparked by the constitutional court decision," said Nazmi Sarikaya from Disbank. "The market was already nervous in the past few days due to rumours of a possible downgrading expected in Turkey's credit rating soon."
Several brokers expect an upward reaction on Friday, with the help of selective buys based on year-end profit prospects.

"The index met support at 90,500 during today's fall, but it may ease towards 87,000 in the medium term if it cannot exceed the 92,500 mark tomorrow," Murat Emrali from Eczacibasi securities told Reuters.
Other brokers said the index could drift sideways between 90,000 and 92,000 for a while.
